subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I should keep this economical but reasonably rich, aiming for a manageable module length. For the vehicle, I'll keep it static without joints since props and scenery can be plain objects, and rigged models need exactly one root bone if I decide to add any moving parts later.

I'm sketching out dimensions: a carrier roughly 9m long and 3m wide, with wheels around 0.65-0.7 radius, facing +Z as the front. The railgun barrel points forward and tilts up slightly, with four deployable outrigger legs reaching the ground for stability while the wheels also stay grounded. I'm planning helper functions for boxes and cylinders to build the chassis, wheels, axles, and hubs, laying wheels out in three pairs along the hull length.

Now I'm extruding the hull's upper deck using a sloped side profile, then building a separate cab section at the front with an angled windscreen using its own extrusion outline.

Positioning tilted glass boxes...

I'm planning the cockpit visor plane oriented with an outward normal, giving it a teal gradient SVG texture with a divider for a glass look, plus side windows. For the rear, I'm adding a power plant box with vent grills and cooling fins between z -4 and -2.5, then starting to think about railgun mounting.

Now I'm placing the railgun turret on the mid-rear deck with a ring base, turret body dimensions, and twin barrel rails elevated at 25 degrees so they clear the cab, including spacer blocks and glowing cyan coil rings along the barrels.

For coils I'll use torus geometry oriented along the barrel axis with cyan glow accents, plus capacitor housings nearby. For the stabiliser legs, I'm placing four at the chassis corners between the wheel positions, with horizontal arms extending outward and diagonal hydraulic cylinders angling down to ground pads.

Still writing leg geometry...

I'm positioning fender boxes over each wheel arch, checking that the hull width and wheel radius don't overlap incorrectly, and setting up the wheel cylinders with 12-sided geometry and flat faces.

For tire detail, I'm considering adding tread lugs around each wheel using small boxes -- about 12 per wheel across 6 wheels, which stays within the part budget.

For the color palette, I'm picking olive drab, dark charcoal, tan, orange/yellow accents, and a cyan glow for lights, with steel tones for metal paint, and considering using the panelled and camo-patch helpers from the clockwork kit to texture the hull.

I'm planning several supporting svg textures — visor glass, a hull emblem decal ("RG-6" with a star), hazard stripes for legs and bumper, a radiator grille, hub detail, glowing display screens, and a warning label — and working out how to apply the hull decal so it reads correctly on both sides by flipping its direction vector.

Now I'm sketching the rest of the vehicle's details: roof antenna, light bar, rear exhaust stacks, tow hooks, glowing headlights, side capacitor/ammo boxes, a sensor mast, ladder, and a banded row of capacitor cylinders on the rear deck, plus beginning the turret's base cylinder and body extrusion profile.

Shaping turret geometry...

The rear of the rail stays inside the turret body, slightly embedded near the top, so I'll keep the breech block protruding there which looks fine. Checking the muzzle end: it extends out to about 7.3m in z and 6.4m in y, giving a total length around 11.5m and height 6.5m, which clears the cab roof without collision.

I'm lowering the elevation angle to 18° to reduce the overall height to roughly 5.8m. Now I'm defining the rail's cross-section geometry—steel rail boxes, the glowing cyan insulator strip between them, periodic mounting blocks along the rail length, and coil rings as thin torus shapes spaced along the barrel axis.

For the coil rings, I'm checking that a box-frame alternative might read better as blocky geometry than a circular torus, so I'm switching to a four-bar square frame with octagonal tube segments to enclose the rails cleanly. I'm also planning the muzzle brake with a glowing slit and heat shield, and setting up helper vectors (direction and normal along the barrel) to position parts relative to the barrel's curve.

For bone orientation, I'm working out that local +X maps to world -X for symmetric placement, while local Z follows the forward direction, and I'll use "z" as the aim axis for the torus so it stays symmetric. Next I'm adding turret details: skirt armor, a cupola, hatch cylinders, a sensor box with lens glow, ladder rungs, ammo boxes, and rear-deck capacitor cylinders.

For the rear deck, I'm placing a power housing box with a radiator grille on its back face and top vents, plus two vertical exhaust stacks positioned symmetrically on either side, rather than a row of capacitor cylinders.

Now I'm shifting attention to the front: a bumper with hazard striping, glowing headlights, a winch, tow hooks, and a grille, positioning the front hull and cab faces at the appropriate z-depths.

I'm also working out the underbody, adding a dark skid plate beneath the hull between the wheel wells, respecting ground clearance, and placing axle beams connecting each wheel.

For the stabilizer legs, I'm deciding to keep hazard-stripe texture only on a short sleeve segment rather than the whole arm, so the main arm stays olive-colored. I'm planning the leg mount blocks on the hull sides, positioning four legs in front and rear pairs along the hull length.

Now I'm working out the geometry for each leg assembly: an angled beam from the hull mount outward, a piston-style rod with wider upper and narrower lower sections, and a small cylindrical foot pad at the base.

Skipping those ribs for now and moving on to overall width check at 7.4m, then planning cab details like side window planes, mirrors, roof light bar, antenna, and a sensor dome, plus side skirts over wheels while skipping extra stowage lockers. Now starting to write the helper functions for the geometry.

Writing box helper function...

I'm setting up the camo paint patterns, using a mottled olive color scheme with small-scale variation for the armor plating.

I'm checking texel density for the paint sheet relative to the model's scale, figuring seams around 2.5mm would be nearly subpixel at 1024 texels but bumping to 2048 gets closer to 1cm resolution, which should still render faint but acceptable seam lines. Mud wear at the bottom looks good, so I'll move on to the texture SVGs.

Now I'm sketching out the decal set: a teal gradient visor with diagonal highlights and a frame, a roundel emblem with a star and "RG-6" stencil text, yellow-black hazard stripes as a repeating pattern, a dark vent grille with frame, a wheel hub with bolt circles mapped onto the hub geometry, a glowing cyan status screen reading "CHARGE 87%" for the turret's control panel, and a warning triangle decal with a lightning bolt for the capacitor.

Now I'm working out the glow placement across parts like the rail strip, coils, headlights, screen, and light bar, plus the exact wheel assembly geometry — hub caps, tire cylinders, gray rims, and positioning math to align everything flush on each side.

For the tire detail, I'm adding lugs around each wheel, placing 14 boxes radially spaced around the tire face and figuring out the rotation math so each lug orients correctly along the radial direction using directional vectors instead of raw angles.

Checking the lug radius against the tire radius confirms the bottom lug only sinks about 2cm into the ground, which is negligible, so I'll switch to 16 lugs and adjust the angular offset accordingly.

Now I'm moving on to the mudguards, then the cab details like a vision slit, before working on the rear hull—adding a bumper, tow lug, and glowing taillights, plus placing a grille near the rear power housing at the correct z-depth so it sits just behind the housing without clipping the hull.

Shifting to the hull profile itself, I'm defining the top surface across the rear-to-mid section with a sloped front edge, then fitting the cab on top starting where the hood ends, making sure the cab's front face aligns with the hull's front lip and includes a lower vertical section for the grille and headlights.

Now I'm placing headlight boxes and a grille texture plane near the front, double-checking that the hull's front slope and cab base don't clash, and considering side emblem placement -- but realizing the leg arms sitting at z ±1.4 would block decals placed between the front and rear wheel wells.

I'm reworking emblem and number placement: moving emblems to the turret sides instead of the hull, planning windows on the cab between z 3.0-3.8, and adding a small "07" marking near the cab door above the window line. Now starting to write the decal placement code for the turret emblem.

Also sketching extra turret details: an eye-like sensor housing, a hatch cylinder with a grab handle near the top, and thin antenna whips rising from the rear corner of the turret.

For the barrel, I'm adding recoil buffer cylinders beneath the rails, a cradle box wrapping the barrel, and a dark steel mantlet box at the turret front face. I'll skip the unused rng import to avoid typecheck errors.

Setting up imports from the builder library and metal paint helpers, then defining a camo paint function using noise and smoothstep to blend olive and base colors across the surface.

Still blending terrain colors...

Adding box and cylinder helper functions...

Skipping the sides option and keeping default smoothness for the rod. Now I'm setting up the barrel geometry with an elevation angle, computing direction and normal vectors from the pivot point, then building the two side rails as boxes spanning along the barrel direction out to the muzzle.

Still writing barrel details...

Interleaving block and coil positions along the barrel, then adding a muzzle box with a glow slit, a dark breech block, and considering recoil buffer cylinders mounted underneath to avoid clashing with the turret top.

Now I'm finishing up the small details: identification bands on the barrel, a rod antenna, an amber light bar on the cab roof, and a lathe-profile sensor dome mounted on the roof.

Next I'm setting up the cab and hull using extrusions with set thicknesses and colors, then positioning an angled windscreen plane oriented to match the cab's slope, giving it a visor-style texture.

Moving on to defining the side windows...

I'm checking the cab's sloped roofline carefully so the side window placement doesn't clip into the angled surface, adjusting the window's z-position and width until the geometry fits cleanly within the slope.

Now I'm placing the headlights, grille, and bumper with a hazard-striped texture at the front of the hull, positioning each element to sit flush against the bumper and body panels.

Then I'm figuring out the fenders and wheel arch lips, checking their positions against the wheel geometry and leg supports to make sure nothing overlaps at the front and rear wheel locations.

Next I'm adding the underbody skid plate positioned below the hull, plus cylindrical axles and spherical differentials connecting the wheels. Then I'm placing small glowing taillight boxes and a rear hazard bumper strip before moving on to the power housing block.

Now I'm shaping the power housing details: a grille plane on the back face, a dark top vent box, and a pair of exhaust cylinders mounted near the top, finishing with a conical cap.

Then I'm adding some hull-side storage boxes positioned to avoid the turret ring, placing them in a gap near the cab, and finally setting up the turret ring itself as a 12-segment dark cylinder before starting the turret body.

Working out the turret extrusion profile and mantlet placement, I settle on a front mantlet box sized to fit the slope without clipping, then add a glowing screen panel on the turret side.

Now I'm adding warning decals on the housing sides, emblem markers on the turret, and a small number plate near the cab window, checking the z-ranges so they don't overlap the glass. Then I'm planning antenna rods on the turret rear and a camera pod up front.

Still writing SVG icons, now building out the grille, emblem, visor, and hub elements...

Now I'm finishing the leg geometry loop and verifying the part helper signature accepts position, direction, axis, texture, and flat options before writing the final code.
